title: Homotopy equivalence for localized polynomial presentations
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, let $R=A[V]\twoheadrightarrow B$ be a surjective $A$-algebra map on any set $V$ of variables, and let $P=W^{-1}A[E]\twoheadrightarrow B$ be another surjective $A$-algebra map on any set $E$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Here $W$ is a multiplicative subset containing $1$ and closed under multiplication, and $W^{-1}A[E]$ is the ring of fractions $f/w$, with $f/w=g/v$ exactly when $u(vf-wg)=0$ for some $u\in W$. Put $I=\ker(R\to B)$, $J=\ker(P\to B)$, and define $N(R)=[I/I^2\xrightarrow{\delta_R}\Omega^1_{R/A}\otimes_RB]$ and $N(P)=[J/J^2\xrightarrow{\delta_P}\Omega^1_{P/A}\otimes_PB]$ in degrees $-1,0$, with $\delta([h])=\mathrm dh\otimes1$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. There exists an $A$-algebra map $a:R\to P$ over $B$. For every such $a$, its induced chain map $N(a)$, sending $[h]$ to $[a(h)]$ and $\mathrm dr\otimes b$ to $\mathrm d(a(r))\otimes b$, is a homotopy equivalence. More precisely, there exists an $A$-algebra map $\ell:P\to R/I^2$ reducing to $P\to B$. It induces a $B$-linear chain map $g:N(P)\to N(R)$ whose degree $-1$ map sends $[h]$ to $\ell(h)\in I/I^2$, and whose degree $0$ map sends $\mathrm dp\otimes b$ to $b\overline{\mathrm d}(\ell(p))$, where $\overline{\mathrm d}:R/I^2\to\Omega^1_{R/A}\otimes_RB$ is the derivation induced by $r\mapsto\mathrm dr\otimes1$. There exist $B$-linear maps $H_R:N(R)^0\to N(R)^{-1}$ and $H_P:N(P)^0\to N(P)^{-1}$ with $gN(a)-1=\delta_RH_R+H_R\delta_R$ and $N(a)g-1=\delta_PH_P+H_P\delta_P$, interpreted degreewise. No inverse ring map $P\to R$ is assumed. The assertion includes $W=\{1\}$ and arbitrarily many variables.

source.place: Tag 00S1 (lemma-NL-homotopy), proof of part (4), with Tag 04EG (lemma-localization-formally-etale) for the square-zero lift: extension of the polynomial-presentation argument to localized polynomial presentations.

proof.text: Write $\epsilon_R:R\twoheadrightarrow B$ and $\epsilon_P:P\twoheadrightarrow B$ for the augmentations. Choose for each $v\in V$ a preimage in $P$ of $\epsilon_R(v)$. The polynomial universal property gives $a:R\to P$ over $B$. Fix any such $a$. The arbitrary-surjection chain-map assertion of [lem-trf-conormal-semilinear-difference-homotopy], with both coefficient maps identities, gives exactly the asserted $B$-linear chain map $N(a)$ on the two displayed kinds of generators.

Put $D=R/I^2$, $q_R:R\to D$, and $M=\ker(D\to B)=I/I^2$. Multiplication in $D$ gives $M^2=0$ and the $D$-action on $M$ factors through $B$. Lift the images of the variables $E$ from $B$ to $D$. By [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] this defines $u:A[E]\to D$ lifting $A[E]\to P\to B$. Regard $D$ as an $A[E]$-algebra via $u$, so $D/M\cong B$ compatibly with $A[E]$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-square-zero-lifting] to $A[E]\to W^{-1}A[E]=P$, $D$, and the square-zero ideal $M$, with the given map $P\to B\cong D/M$. It gives $\ell:P\to D$ reducing to $\epsilon_P$. In particular $\ell(J)\subset M$ and $\ell(J^2)=0$.

source.place: Tag 04EG (lemma-localization-formally-etale), square-zero lifting; Tag 00S1 (lemma-NL-homotopy), polynomial-variable lifting in part (1).

proof.text: For $x,y\in I$, the Leibniz identity gives $\mathrm d(xy)\otimes1=x\,\mathrm dy\otimes1+y\,\mathrm dx\otimes1=0$ in $\Omega^1_{R/A}\otimes_RB$. By additivity this derivation annihilates $I^2$ and hence factors through $\overline{\mathrm d}_R:D\to\Omega^1_{R/A}\otimes_RB$. The identical calculation with $J\subset P$ gives $\overline{\mathrm d}_P:P/J^2\to\Omega^1_{P/A}\otimes_PB$. Their restrictions to $M=I/I^2$ and $J/J^2$ are respectively $\delta_R$ and $\delta_P$, by evaluating a representative. These are derivations for the module actions through $B$.

The restriction of $\ell$ gives $g^{-1}:J/J^2\to M$: it is well defined since $\ell(J^2)=0$. It is $B$-linear since for $p\in P$ and $h\in J$, $\ell(ph)=\ell(p)\ell(h)=\epsilon_P(p)\ell(h)$ in the square-zero ideal $M$. The composite $\overline{\mathrm d}_R\ell$ is an $A$-derivation with $P$ acting through $B$. By the universal property of differentials it defines $g^0(\mathrm dp\otimes b)=b\overline{\mathrm d}_R(\ell(p))$. On $[h]\in J/J^2$ both $\delta_Rg^{-1}([h])$ and $g^0\delta_P([h])$ equal $\overline{\mathrm d}_R(\ell(h))$. Thus $g$ is the required chain map.

source.place: Tag 00RO (lemma-universal-omega); Tag 00S1 (lemma-NL-homotopy), chain-map formulas with a lift modulo the squared kernel.

proof.text: Choose an $A$-algebra map $t:R\to R$ lifting $\ell a:R\to D$, by lifting each variable through $q_R$ and using the polynomial universal property. Then $t$ lies over $B$. For $i\in I$, $[t(i)]=\ell(a(i))=g^{-1}N(a)^{-1}([i])$ in $M$. For $r\in R$, $\mathrm dt(r)\otimes1=\overline{\mathrm d}_R(\ell(a(r)))=g^0N(a)^0(\mathrm dr\otimes1)$, by step 3. Hence $N(t)=gN(a)$. Apply [lem-trf-conormal-semilinear-difference-homotopy] to $t$ and $1_R$ to obtain $H_R(\mathrm dr\otimes b)=b[t(r)-r]$, with $(gN(a))^{-1}-1=H_R\delta_R$ in degree $-1$ and $(gN(a))^0-1=\delta_RH_R$ in degree $0$. Superscripts $-1$ denote degree components, not inverse maps.

source.place: Tag 00S1 (lemma-NL-homotopy), part (2), applied to two actual maps out of the polynomial presentation.

proof.text: Since $a(I^2)\subset J^2$, $a$ induces $\bar a:D\to P/J^2$. Put $q_P:P\to P/J^2$ and $D_P=\bar a\ell-q_P:P\to J/J^2$. It is additive, vanishes on $A$, and satisfies $D_P(pp\prime)=\epsilon_P(p)D_P(p\prime)+\epsilon_P(p\prime)D_P(p)$: expand the product using $\bar a\ell=q_P+D_P$ and use $(J/J^2)^2=0$. Thus the universal property gives a $B$-linear $H_P$ with $H_P(\mathrm dp\otimes b)=bD_P(p)$.

source.place: Tags 00RO (lemma-universal-omega) and 00S1 (lemma-NL-homotopy), difference-derivation calculation in part (2).

proof.text: For $h\in J$, $H_P\delta_P([h])=D_P(h)=N(a)^{-1}g^{-1}([h])-[h]$. For the other degree, evaluate $\overline{\mathrm d}_P\bar a=N(a)^0\overline{\mathrm d}_R$ on $q_R(r)$: both sides equal $\mathrm d(a(r))\otimes1$, so they agree on every element of $D$. Consequently $\delta_PH_P(\mathrm dp\otimes b)=b\overline{\mathrm d}_P(\bar a\ell(p)-q_P(p))=N(a)^0g^0(\mathrm dp\otimes b)-\mathrm dp\otimes b$. These generator equalities give $N(a)g-1=\delta_PH_P+H_P\delta_P$ degreewise. Together with step 5 they prove the homotopy equivalence. The construction works for arbitrary sets $V,E$ and for $W=\{1\}$; it requires only $P\to R/I^2$, never $P\to R$.
